corpus.rationale: Not an exact duplicate. organ-document-service overlaps on the document-classification decision but derives from a DISTINCT source service (app/services/document_service.py, the Stream 09 `Document`/documents-table API+worker pipeline), whereas this organ derives from app/services/document_ingestion.py (the `UploadedDocument`/uploaded_documents discovery-upload pipeline). The unique routing here (extraction-method dispatch, target-project selection, idempotency on facts_extracted, 50k truncation cap, next_status state machine) has no counterpart in organ-document-service, which instead owns filename-keyword classification, fact-extraction theme hints, and extraction-readiness. Overlap flagged for operator dedup awareness; the two map to two genuinely separate Flask pipelines so neither is redundant today.

oss.rationale: No permissive OSS library supersedes this organ. The 2026 OSS document market (Tesseract, PaddleOCR, dots.ocr, unstructured.io, Apache Tika, Docling, MistralOCR, olmOCR) operates at the IMPURE I/O layer: actual text extraction and ML-based classification. This organ is the PURE routing/decision layer extracted FROM the Flask service precisely so the impure parts stay there. Its value is bespoke business logic bound to discovery-engine's UploadedDocument state machine, tenant-project routing, allowed-classification normalisation, idempotency, and truncation cap, none of which an OSS extractor provides. The impure extraction the Flask service performs (pypdf / python-docx / OCR) is already the correct home for OSS adoption; the decision organ stays.
